fixes.what: The dossier draws continuous Grimaldi rule over the Rock from 1297 to 1641, but the Grimaldi lost the Rock to Genoa four times before 1419 (and to Milan briefly in 1436); the ledger has none of these losses and regains and keyframes 0-2 hold the Rock throughout.
fixes.why: Monaco page (source[0], opened by the author): 'Francesco was evicted a few years later by the Genoese forces, and the struggle over "the Rock" continued for another century'; 'The House of Grimaldi has ruled Monaco, with brief interruptions, since 1297'; 'in the late 1300s Genoa lost Monaco after fighting the Crown of Aragon'; 'In 1419, the Grimaldi family purchased Monaco from the Crown of Aragon and became the official and undisputed rulers'. List of rulers of Monaco: 'Under Genoese control from 10 April 1301 to 12 September 1331'; Charles I 'retook the Rock from the Genoese'; Rainier II 'Yielded Monaco to the besieging Genoese for 20,000 fl. but retained Menton and Roquebrune'; 'Under Genoese control from 15 August 1357 to January 1395'; 'from 19 December 1395 to 11 May 1397'; 'from 5 November 1402 to 5 June 1419'; Jean, Ambroise and Antoine 'bought back Monaco from Genoa'; 'Monaco was occupied by the Duchy of Milan ... from 3 October to November 1436'. Keyframe 0's note 'Under Genoese sovereignty until the Spanish authority of 1524' is also contradicted by the Monaco page's Aragonese period.
fixes.fix: Add, citing List of rulers of Monaco (add it to sources): loss 1301-04 to republic-of-genoa {country: Monaco} (the Rock); gain 1331-09 from republic-of-genoa; loss 1357-08 to republic-of-genoa (the Rock only, Menton and Roquebrune kept); gain 1395-01; loss 1395-12; gain 1397-05; loss 1402-11; gain 1419-06 (counterpart republic-of-genoa per the list, note that the Monaco page names the Crown of Aragon as seller; pick one and record the disagreement); occupation_start 1436-10 and occupation_end 1436-11 with duchy-of-milan. Split the new keyframes to match: Rock 1297-1300; no keyframe 1301-1330 (or move start/found to 1331-09 if the project prefers, saying so); Rock 1331-1345; plus Menton 1346-1354; three places 1355-1356; Menton and Roquebrune only 1357-1394, 1396 and 1402-1418; three places 1395, 1397-1401 and 1419-1641. Fix keyframe 0's sovereignty note (Genoa, then Aragon in the late 1300s to 1419), and split or annotate the capital (the seat cannot be the Rock while Genoa held it; say where the lords sat, or that the page is silent).
